title: Windsurf everywhere, doing everything, all at once - Kevin Hou, Windsurf

primary.label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 98%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk focuses on Windsurf, an IDE-based coding agent that generates, reviews, and ships software, including the purpose-built SWE-1 model trained for software engineering workflows rather than pure code generation.

summary: Kevin Hou opens by establishing Windsurf's rapid growth: millions of users, 90 million lines of code generated daily, over a thousand messages per minute, and 10 product waves since the November 2024 launch (retiring the Kodium name). He reveals Windsurf's core philosophy—a shared timeline between human and AI that creates the feeling of mind-reading, evolving from pre-autocomplete through Copilot-era edits to multi-file agentic capabilities. Hou identifies three context categories developers need: coding-related file reads and terminal actions, external sources like GitHub and web docs, and metalearning (organizational best practices). He illustrates a concrete workflow from Slack to Google Docs to Jira to Figma to coding to PRs to deploys, motivating Windsurf Everywhere (reading context from all sources via MCP) and Windsurf Doing Everything (taking actions including terminal commands, browser previews, GitHub PRs, code reviews, and one-click Netlify deploys). The third pillar, Windsurf On All the Time, targets moving from 80-90% agent / 10-20% human timelines toward 99% agent / 1% human. Hou argues this timeline problem differs fundamentally from SWE-bench, requiring a purpose-built model. He introduces SWE-1, trained for entire software engineering workflows using End-to-End Task and Conversational SWE Task benchmarks. SWE-1 achieves near-frontier model results at a fraction of the cost with a significantly smaller team, and users choose it at higher frequency than models like Claude 3.7 and 3.5 because it recognizes how engineers work. Hou describes a data flywheel: ship the best product, users find the frontier through thumbs up/down and accept/reject signals, Windsurf builds at that margin with better models, tools, and agentic harness, then repeats. He closes arguing that building AI products in 2025 demands harmony of model, data, and application, where the application mimics the user behavior the model should replicate.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Growth
sections.summary: Kevin Hou introduces himself as head of product at Windsurf, recounts rapid growth since the November 2024 launch, and highlights 10 waves of innovations including web search, MCP support, auto-generated memories, deploys, and parallel agents. Notes 90 million lines of code generated daily and over a thousand messages per minute.

sections.title: Core Philosophy: Shared Timeline
sections.summary: Reveals Windsurf's secret sauce as a shared timeline between human and AI. Traces evolution from pre-autocomplete through Copilot-era small edits to Windsurf's multi-file agentic capabilities launched in late 2024. Emphasizes the timeline must handle actions beyond the IDE.

sections.title: Windsurf Everywhere: Context Ingestion
sections.summary: Defines three context categories: coding-related file reads and terminal actions, external sources like GitHub and web docs, and metalearning (organizational best practices). Walks through a concrete example of building a dashboard page spanning Slack, Google Docs, Jira, Figma, and coding. Highlights MCP connectivity to Notion, Linear, Stripe, and others.

sections.title: Windsurf Doing Everything: Beyond Coding
sections.summary: Describes Windsurf's expansion to actions beyond code: intelligent terminal command execution with selective user approval, browser previews for visual iteration, GitHub MCP for PRs with context-informed descriptions, Windsurf reviews for automated code review, and one-click Netlify deployment.

sections.title: Windsurf On All the Time: Autonomous Future
sections.summary: Articulates the vision of moving from 80-90% agent timelines to 99% agent / 1% human, with background research and autonomous work. Envisions coding anytime, anywhere, including voice-activated scenarios. Frames the timeline problem as fundamentally different from competitive programming.

sections.title: SWE-1 Model and Benchmarks
sections.summary: Introduces SWE-1, a custom software engineering model trained for entire workflows, not just code generation. Describes two benchmarks: End-to-End Task Benchmark (completing pull requests) and Conversational SWE Task Benchmark (assisting mid-workflow), the latter fitting Windsurf's mid-timeline assistance paradigm.

sections.title: SWE-1 Results and the Data Flywheel
sections.summary: Reports that SWE-1 achieves near-frontier model results at a fraction of the cost with a significantly smaller team. Users choose SWE-1 in the model dropdown at higher frequency than Claude 3.7 and 3.5 because it recognizes how they work. Describes a data flywheel: ship the best product, users find the frontier via thumbs up/down and accept/reject, Windsurf builds at the margin with better models and tools, and repeats. Closes arguing that AI products in 2025 demand harmony of model, data, and application, where the application mimics the user behavior to replicate in the model. Hou invites engineers to try Windsurf and notes the company is hiring.
